method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Cholera' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Routine cholera vaccination of travellers is NOT recommended — the risk to travellers is very low**, even though cholera is endemic in some countries Australians visit. It is for **travellers at high risk of exposure**.
claims.source_text: Routine cholera vaccination of travellers is not recommended. The risk to travellers is very low, despite cholera being endemic in some countries that Australians visit.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Cholera', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/cholera, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral inactivated (Dukoral) or live (Vaxchora) — no preference in the immunocompetent.** ⚠️ **The immunocompromised, or anyone on immunosuppressive treatment, must use the oral INACTIVATED vaccine.**
claims.source_text: Dukoral, or the live cholera vaccine, Vaxchora, can be used. There is no preference for either vaccine in immunocompetent people. People who are immunocompromised, or people receiving immunosuppressive drugs or treatments should use the oral inactivated cholera vaccine.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Cholera', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/cholera, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children 2–6: 1 dose of live vaccine, OR 3 doses of inactivated.**
claims.source_text: Children aged 2-6 years are recommended to receive either 1 dose of live attenuated cholera vaccine, or 3 doses of inactivated cholera vaccine.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Cholera', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/cholera, retrieved 2026-09-23
